items.stem: Which statement about a Python generator function (one that uses yield) is correct?

options.text: It produces values lazily, one at a time, and keeps its state between calls
options.rationale: Correct: a generator suspends at each yield and resumes on the next request, producing values on demand.

options.text: It returns a list of all values immediately
options.rationale: That describes a function returning a list; a generator yields values lazily, not all at once.

options.text: It can be re-iterated any number of times after exhaustion
options.rationale: A generator is exhausted after one pass and must be recreated to iterate again.

options.text: It cannot be used in a for loop
options.rationale: Generators are iterable and are commonly consumed by for loops.

items.explanation: Correct: a generator suspends at each yield and resumes on the next request, producing values on demand.

items.stem: In a class, what does the first parameter conventionally named self refer to?

options.text: The particular instance the method was called on
options.rationale: Correct: self is the instance, giving the method access to that object's attributes.
The class object is referenced by cls in classmethods, not by self.
The base class is reached via super(), not self.

options.text: A required keyword of the language
options.rationale: self is a convention, not a keyword; any valid name would work but self is standard.

items.explanation: Correct: self is the instance, giving the method access to that object's attributes.

items.stem: Which TWO are true about the try/except/finally construct?

options.text: Code in a finally block runs whether or not an exception was raised
options.rationale: Correct: finally always executes, making it ideal for cleanup such as closing files.

options.text: A single try can have several except branches for different exception types
options.rationale: Correct: you can match distinct exception classes with separate except clauses.

options.text: The else block of a try runs only when an exception was raised
options.rationale: The else block runs only when NO exception was raised in the try.

options.text: Raising an exception in except is forbidden
options.rationale: You may raise (or re-raise) inside an except block.

options.text: finally can only appear without any except
options.rationale: finally may accompany except clauses in the same statement.

items.explanation: Correct: finally always executes, making it ideal for cleanup such as closing files.
